question: What is the difference between RAM and storage?

avant_2b.réponse: RAM (Random Access Memory) holds active data temporarily while Storage stores permanent files and programs on hard drives or SSDs. Both are essential components of a computer system, but RAM speeds up processing speed, whereas Storage saves your work for later use.

apres_2b.réponse: RAM (Random Access Memory) acts as temporary, volatile workspace where your computer instantly loads active programs and data for fast processing, while storage like SSDs or HDDs serves as permanent, non-volatile backup holding files and software indefinitely. For instance, if you close a browser tab, the image in RAM disappears immediately, but it remains on your hard drive until you reopen the app.

apres_4b.réponse: RAM acts like a fast temporary workspace where your computer keeps active data for quick access, while storage is like a large, slower archive that holds everything permanently. For example, when you open a game, it loads into RAM to run smoothly but saves the actual game files on your hard drive or SSD so they aren't lost when you turn off the computer.

question: Which one loses its contents when I power off?

avant_2b.réponse: RAM loses all data immediately when you power off, while Storage retains your files and programs until they are explicitly deleted or overwritten by new data.

apres_2b.réponse: RAM loses all active data instantly when you turn off power because it is volatile memory designed for temporary use only. In contrast, storage like an SSD or HDD retains your files and programs even after the device shuts down, as long as the power remains on until a reboot occurs.

apres_4b.réponse: RAM loses all its data immediately when you power off, whereas storage retains your files even after a shutdown. Think of RAM as an empty desk that disappears when you leave the room, while storage is like a locked filing cabinet that stays closed and safe.

question: Quelle est la différence entre un compilateur et un interpréteur ?

apres_2b.réponse: Un compilateur transforme le code source en machine code exécutable immédiatement, tandis qu'un interpréteur exécute ligne par ligne le code source sans le traduire à l'avance. Par exemple, Python est interprété, mais C++ est compilé.

apres_4b.réponse: Un compilateur traduit tout le code entier en langage machine avant l'exécution, tandis qu'un interpréteur exécute le code ligne par ligne au fur et à mesure. Par exemple, Java utilise d'abord un compilateur pour créer du bytecode, puis un interpréteur (JVM) qui le lit et le transforme en instructions réelles.
